value.question_text: Show a proof that the decision form of Independent Set is NP-complete.

blocks.text: 1. Show that INDEPENDENT SET is in NP.

Nondeterministically guess some subset of the vertices. If this set is at least of size k (k is the parameter to the decision problem), and the vertices are all independent, then return YES. Otherwise return NO.
Nondeterministically guess some collection of vertices. If the vertices are independent, and if it is the biggest such set, then return YES. Otherwise return NO.
1. Show that INDEPENDENT SET is NP-hard by using a reduction $\$ of known NP-complete problem CLIQUE to IS.
1. Show that INDEPENDENT SET is NP-hard by using a reduction $\$ of IS to known NP-complete problem CLIQUE.
Show transformations to reduce CLIQUE to IS.
Show transformations to reduce IS to CLIQUE.
To reduce a CLIQUE input instance to an IS input instance for a given graph $G = (V , E)$, construct a complementary graph $G’ = (V’ , E’)$ such that:
To reduce an IS input instance to a CLIQUE input instance for a given graph $G = (V , E)$, construct a complementary graph $G’ = (V’ , E’)$ such that:
a. $V = V’$. That is, the complement graph will have the same vertices as the original graph.
b. $E’$ is the complement of $E$ that is $G’$ has all the edges that is $\textbf{not}$ present in $G$.
Construction of the complementary graph can be done in polynomial time.
We need to show that with this reduction, there is an independent set of size k in the complement graph if and only iff there exists a clique of size k in G.

$\textbf{If there is an independent set of size $k$ in the complement graph $G’$}$, it implies no two vertices share an edge in $G’$, which further implies all of those vertices share an edge with all others in $G$ forming a clique. That is, $\textbf{there exists a clique of size $k$ in $G$}$.

$\textbf{If there is a clique of size $k$ in the graph $G$}$, it implies all vertices share an edge with all others in $G$, which further implies no two of these vertices share an edge in $G’$ (thus forming an Independent Set. That is, $\textbf{there exists an independent set of size $k$ in $G’$}$.
